lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

recently_moved_to_uk.description: Whether the claimant has recently moved to the UK.

right_to_reside_status.description: A plain English description of the claimant's right-to-reside position.

I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 3 years old and lives at home with me. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Let me ask you a few more questions to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do live in the UK. Though I should mention, we've only recently moved here.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming. Since you've recently moved to the UK, I need to ask a few more questions about your circumstances.

**What is your immigration or residency status in the UK?** For example, are you:
- A British citizen
- An EU/EEA/Swiss national (and if so, do you have settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme)
- Someone who has moved to the UK with the right to reside
- Or another status?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not entirely sure about all the technical terms to be honest. I know we have the right to be here, but I'm not certain about the exact status or what it's called officially. Is that going to be a problem?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's perfectly alright - I understand the terminology can be confusing. Let me help you figure this out with some simpler questions.

**Can you tell me where you moved from, and do you have any documentation about your right to live in the UK?** For example:
- Did you move from another European country?
- Are you a British citizen or do you have British citizenship?
- Do you have a visa or any paperwork that allows you to stay in the UK?
- Or were you born in the UK?

Any information you can share will help me understand your situation better.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: We moved here from overseas - not from Europe. I do have paperwork that allows us to stay here legally, but I don't really understand all the details of what my exact status is or what category it falls under. I know we're allowed to be here though. Does that make sense?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Yes, that makes sense, thank you for explaining. Since you moved from overseas (not from Europe) and have paperwork allowing you to stay legally in the UK, your eligibility for Child Benefit will depend on whether you have "right to reside" in the UK.

**Are you currently working in the UK, or are you planning to work?** If so, what type of work are you doing or looking to do?

This will help me understand if you meet the requirements for claiming Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent

Since you moved to the UK from overseas (non-EU) for family reasons, have paperwork allowing you to stay, you're not currently working, and it's just you and Alex, I need to understand a bit more about your legal status to determine eligibility.
